lines.cap: This horse could do maths. Or could he?
lines.say: This horse could do maths. Or could he?

lines.cap: Berlin, around 1904. A teacher shows off his horse, Hans, to amazed crowds.
lines.say: Berlin, around 1904. A teacher shows off his horse, Hans, to amazed crowds.

lines.cap: Ask him two plus three, and Hans taps his hoof. One, two, three, four, five. Then stops.
lines.say: Ask him two plus three, and Hans taps his hoof. One, two, three, four, five. Then stops.

lines.cap: He could add, tell the time, even spell. Newspapers called him Clever Hans.
lines.say: He could add, tell the time, even spell. Newspapers called him Clever Hans.

lines.cap: A psychologist, Oskar Pfungst, ran a test. What if the person asking doesn't know the answer?
lines.say: A psychologist, Oskar Pfungst, ran a test. What if the person asking doesn't know the answer?

lines.cap: Suddenly, Hans got almost everything wrong.
lines.say: Suddenly, Hans got almost everything wrong.

lines.cap: Hans wasn't counting. He was reading faces. When he reached the right number, people relaxed without knowing it. And Hans stopped.
lines.say: Hans wasn't counting. He was reading faces. When he reached the right number, people relaxed without knowing it. And Hans stopped.

lines.cap: Today, scientists still blind their experiments, because of a horse.
lines.say: Today, scientists still blind their experiments, because of a horse.

lines.cap: He couldn't do maths. He could read you.
lines.say: He couldn't do maths. He could read you.
